samples.summary: Autofit commit now anchors the unrotated top-left, but the live in-place editor and canvas underlay still grow with x/y fixed — a rotated text box jumps at commit instead of at re-render
samples.evidence:
The commit path (editor.ts:4431) computes `resizeFrameToSize(localFrame, localFrame.w, targetH)` and writes the compensated x/y. The two surfaces that show the box WHILE editing were not updated to the same anchor:
- `maskEditingElement` (editor.ts:7434-7437) builds the live underlay frame as `{ ...el.frame, h: Math.max(MIN_TEXT_BOX_H, liveHeight) }` — h only, x/y untouched, i.e. exactly the size-only patch this delta replaced.
- the DOM editing container (text-box-editor.ts:331-334, 344-347, 493) is positioned at `frame.x/y`, rotated with `transform-origin: center`, and only its `style.height` grows; the pivot therefore moves with the growing box.
So during typing the rotated box is painted/rotated about the NEW centre of `(x, y, w, h')`, while on commit the element lands at the anchored x/y. The two placements differ by |(0,Δh/2) − R(0,Δh/2)|, which for a substantially rotated box is on the order of the height growth — a visible snap at the moment the editor detaches. Reachable in normal use: rotate a text box, double-click, type until it grows.

samples.summary: Commit writes x/y derived from the frame snapshot captured at enter-edit, so a concurrent (remote/collab) move of the element is silently reverted
samples.evidence: `const localFrame = localElement.frame;` is captured at enter-edit (editor.ts:4293) and used inside `onCommit` (editor.ts:4431) to compute `fit.x/fit.y`, which are then written via `updateElementFrame` (editor.ts:4432-4436). `updateElementFrame` merges the patch into the CURRENT frame (store/memory.ts:708), so any position change that happened between enter-edit and commit — a remote peer moving the box in a Yorkie-backed session, which can run for the whole duration of a typing session — is overwritten by the stale-derived coordinates. Before this delta only `h` was patched, so position was never clobbered; the delta newly broadens the write to x/y. The fix is to re-read the element's frame inside the commit batch rather than using the enter-time snapshot.

samples.summary: The new non-finite guard degrades to `return patch`, which still persists the NaN w/h the comment claims it protects against
samples.evidence: `if (!Number.isFinite(next.x) || !Number.isFinite(next.y)) return patch;` — the doc comment above says this covers "a `w`/`h` that arrived as NaN ... rather than writing garbage coordinates". But the only way `next.x/y` become non-finite with a well-formed frame is a non-finite `patch.w`/`patch.h`, and the fallback returns that very patch, which `updateElementFrame` merges into the frame (packages/slides/src/store/memory.ts:708) — persisting `w: NaN` and vanishing the element anyway. A guard that means to reject garbage input should drop the size keys (or bail entirely), not just the compensation. Contained today only because the panel's own `Number.isFinite` check on parseFloat (size-position-section.tsx:273) makes NaN unreachable from the UI — i.e. the guard is defensive and currently ineffective in the one case it names.

verdict.reason: All cited code exists exactly as described. editor.ts:4431-4436 commits the autofit height through resizeFrameToSize, which anchors the unrotated NW corner (resize.ts:127-131 -> frameAtAnchor(start,'se',...)) and thus shifts the rotation centre by R(theta)*(0, dh/2). The two surfaces shown while editing were not updated: maskEditingElement (editor.ts:7434-7437) still patches h only, leaving x/y fixed, and it is driven live on every height report (editor.ts:1537-1542, 4396-4398); the DOM editing container is placed at frame.x/y (text-box-editor.ts:331-334), rotated with transform-origin center (text-box-editor.ts:344-347), and only its height grows (text-box-editor.ts:493-495), so its pivot moves with the box. The grow gate editingGrowApplicable = kind === 'text' && !ancestorHasTransform (editor.ts:4304) compares world vs local frames (editor.ts:4295-4298), so a top-level ROTATED text box passes it — no guard excludes rotation. Net effect: during typing the box paints about the new centre of (x,y,w,h'), while at commit it lands at the anchored x/y; the placements differ by |(0,dh/2) - R(0,dh/2)| = |dh|*|sin(theta/2)| (~0.71*dh at 90 degrees), a visible snap when the editor detaches. Reachable in normal use (rotate a text box, double-click, type until it grows). The design doc enumerates the writers routed through the anchor rule but never scopes out the live editing surfaces, so no already-guarded or out-of-scope ground applies. Real, wrong behavior on a normally reachable path -> blocking at major under the correctness rubric.

finding.summary: Commit writes x/y derived from the frame snapshot captured at enter-edit, so a concurrent (remote/collab) move of the element is silently reverted
finding.evidence: `const localFrame = localElement.frame;` is captured at enter-edit (editor.ts:4293) and used inside `onCommit` (editor.ts:4431) to compute `fit.x/fit.y`, which are then written via `updateElementFrame` (editor.ts:4432-4436). `updateElementFrame` merges the patch into the CURRENT frame (store/memory.ts:708), so any position change that happened between enter-edit and commit — a remote peer moving the box in a Yorkie-backed session, which can run for the whole duration of a typing session — is overwritten by the stale-derived coordinates. Before this delta only `h` was patched, so position was never clobbered; the delta newly broadens the write to x/y. The fix is to re-read the element's frame inside the commit batch rather than using the enter-time snapshot.

verdict.reason: Verified in the repo: `localFrame` is captured from a one-shot `store.read()` snapshot at enter-edit (editor.ts:4216, :4223, :4293) and used inside the later-firing `onCommit` closure to derive `fit.x/fit.y`, which are written via `updateElementFrame` (editor.ts:4431-4436). Both store implementations merge the patch into the element's CURRENT frame by reassigning a new frame object (memory.ts:708; yorkie-slides-store.ts:1456), so the captured reference is a true stale snapshot, not a live view. `resizeFrameToSize`/`frameAtAnchor` (resize.ts:127-157) returns start.x/start.y unchanged at rotation 0, so the enter-time x/y is written unconditionally, not only in the rotated case the write was added for. Any position change between enter-edit and commit — e.g. a remote peer moving the element in the Yorkie-backed collab store — is clobbered. No guard prevents this: onCommit only checks `cancelled` (:4404) and swallows not-found (:4457-4460), and every exitEditMode/editingElementId site (:1647, :1702, :2460, :2487, :3882, :4106, :4209) exits only on local user actions; nothing re-reads the frame or aborts editing on a remote frame change. Correctness lane (data overwrite / stale-state write) and reachable in normal collaborative use.

finding.summary: Text autofit height commit still patches `h` alone, so a rotated text box keeps jumping (#1039) around the new compensation
finding.evidence: `this.options.store.updateElementFrame(slideId, elementId, { h: targetH })` writes a size-only patch. `resizeFrameToSize`'s own doc-comment (packages/slides/src/view/editor/interactions/resize.ts:117) states "Callers that write `w`/`h` on a rotated frame must go through this (or `resizeFrameWorld`) rather than patching size alone." This call site bypasses it. The guard above it only skips when an ANCESTOR has a transform (`!ancestorHasTransform`); the element's OWN `frame.rotation` is never considered, so editing text in a rotated text element and committing still writes a bare `h`, moving every painted point exactly as #1039 describes. Pre-existing, but it is the sibling of the path this diff fixes and leaves the two disagreeing.

verdict.reason: The finding's central factual claim — that the text-autofit commit writes `updateElementFrame(slideId, elementId, { h: targetH })`, a size-only patch — is not in the repository. editor.ts:4431-4436 routes the commit through `resizeFrameToSize(localFrame, localFrame.w, targetH)` and writes the compensated `x` and `y` together with `h`, with a comment at 4421-4430 explicitly citing #1039 as the reason. The claim that "the element's OWN `frame.rotation` is never considered" is also wrong: `resizeFrameToSize` (resize.ts:127-131) delegates to `frameAtAnchor`, which reads `start.rotation ?? 0` at resize.ts:155-159 and builds the rotation matrix from it, so the element's own rotation drives the x/y compensation. The `!ancestorHasTransform` guard concerns ancestor space (world-vs-local height basis), not the element's rotation, as the comment at 4412-4416 and 4427-4430 states. I enumerated every other bare-`h` write in packages/: only editor.ts:4435 (the compensated write) and editor.ts:7436, which is a render-time `{ ...el.frame, h: ... }` preview object pushed into the masked element list, not a store write; `commitCropFrame` at 2600-2605 writes full x/y/w/h. No size-only store patch on a rotated frame exists on this path, so the described defect has no location.

finding.summary: A frame whose `rotation` is absent at runtime now yields NaN x/y (element vanishes / persisted corruption)
finding.evidence: `resizeFrameToSize` computes `Math.cos(start.rotation)` / `Math.sin(start.rotation)` (resize.ts:145-146). `Frame.rotation` is typed as required, but real documents can lack it — `packages/slides/src/import/pptx/shape.ts:1106` defends with `const rot = frame.rotation ?? 0` and `packages/slides/test/view/editor/image-crop-session.test.ts:30` normalises with `frame.rotation ?? 0`, and the Yorkie store hands back raw document data. With `rotation === undefined` both trig calls are NaN, so `next.x`/`next.y` are NaN and the patch writes NaN x/y into the store — before this change a `{w}` patch never touched x/y and was immune. Defaulting to 0 (`start.rotation ?? 0`) or an early return would remove the hazard.

verdict.reason: The described code does not exist. resize.ts:145-146 are comment lines, not trig calls. `frameAtAnchor` — the sole implementation behind `resizeFrameToSize` (resize.ts:127-131) — normalizes rotation at resize.ts:155 with `const rotation = start.rotation ?? 0;` (with a comment explicitly citing the `Math.cos(undefined)` NaN hazard) and only then calls `Math.cos(rotation)`/`Math.sin(rotation)` at resize.ts:156-157. The sibling entries normalize identically (resize.ts:74, resize.ts:97). Additionally the frontend call site already has the exact early-return the finding asks for: frame-patch.ts:33 returns the unmodified size-only patch when `next.x`/`next.y` are non-finite. Both remedies the finding proposes (`start.rotation ?? 0` and an early return) are already present, so no NaN x/y can reach the store via `anchoredFramePatch`.
